title: Attention in the Tally
story: Beatriz counted bird visits while knowing which feeder held the new seed, and her tallies favoured it. A colleague called the preference obvious. Beatriz disagreed, because she might have watched that feeder longer. She repeated the count with the labels hidden. The gap shrank, so the first result had measured her attention as well as the birds. Bias had to be removed, not defended.

vocabulary.definition: A container that offers seed to birds
A result that seemed to favour one choice
Marks showing which feeder was which
The difference between the two counts
A slant in the method that pushes the result

quiz.question: What did Beatriz know during the first count?
options: Which feeder held the new seed
How to hide every label in advance
That the gap would shrink
That her colleague would disagree
quiz.correctAnswer: Which feeder held the new seed
quiz.explanation: She counted while knowing which feeder held the new seed.
quiz.supportingSentence: Beatriz counted bird visits while knowing which feeder held the new seed, and her tallies favoured it.

quiz.question: How was the second count different?
options: The labels were hidden
A different kind of seed was used
The colleague made the tally
The birds were removed from the garden
quiz.explanation: She repeated the count with the labels hidden.
quiz.supportingSentence: She repeated the count with the labels hidden.

quiz.question: What did the shrinking gap imply about the first result?
options: Part of it came from her attention, not only from the birds
The new seed had lost every effect
Hidden labels attract more visits
The colleague had swapped the feeders
quiz.correctAnswer: Part of it came from her attention, not only from the birds
quiz.explanation: Once she could not see the labels the gap shrank, so the first result had measured her attention as well as the birds.
quiz.supportingSentence: The gap shrank, so the first result had measured her attention as well as the birds.

quiz.question: What is a tally in this passage?
options: A count of the visits she recorded
A label stuck on the new seed
A feeder placed out of sight
A colleague’s spoken opinion
quiz.correctAnswer: A count of the visits she recorded
quiz.explanation: Her tallies favoured the known feeder, so a tally is the count she kept.
quiz.supportingSentence: Beatriz counted bird visits while knowing which feeder held the new seed, and her tallies favoured it.

quiz.question: Why does the writer include the colleague calling the preference obvious?
options: To show the easy explanation Beatriz refused to trust
To prove the second count was unnecessary
To suggest birds cannot be counted
To argue that labels should stay visible
quiz.correctAnswer: To show the easy explanation Beatriz refused to trust
quiz.explanation: The colleague’s “obvious” preference is the reading she tests instead of accepting.
quiz.supportingSentence: A colleague called the preference obvious.
